programme.title: Na Clangairean
programme.desc: Tha na Clangairean airson latha sònraichte a thoirt do Dhràgon Brot air sgàth ‘s gu bheil i cho fialaidh ‘s còir. Tha min dòchas gun obraich seo a-mach math dhaibh. The Clangers would like to organise a special day for Soup Dragon as she is so kind and generous. Hopefully this works out well for them.

programme.title: Creag nam Buthaidean/Puffin Rock
programme.desc: It's early in the morning, and Isabelle and Oona are off to visit Otto before he goes to bed. Pip and Pop are already fast asleep, but they have taken up all the bedding. Oona, Isabelle and Otto split up to find soft, comfy things for Otto to sleep on. Seagull feathers are the hardest to get, but Isabelle is the best flier. She is sure she can do it, but her position as top flier is challenged by Otto. Tha e tràth sa mhadainn, 's tha Iseabail is Oona a' dèanamh air otto mus tèid e innte. Tha Pip is Pop mar tha nan suain, ach tha iad air còir a ghabhail air an stuth-leapa gu lèir.Sgaraidh Oona, Iseabail is Otto gus stuth cofhurtail is bog fhaighinn do dh'Otto 'son cadal air. Itean faoileig an rud 's dorr' a lorg, ach 's e Iseabail an t-itealaiche as fheàrr... tha i deimhinnt' gun tèid aic' air...ach tha a h-inbhe mar shàr-itealaiche ga dhùbhlanachadh le Otto.

programme.title: Creag nam Buthaidean/Puffin Rock
programme.desc: Phoenix has picked up a strange, strong smell after playing with Mossy, and nobody knows where it came from. Phoenix needs a swim to wash it off, and on the way to the river, the friends try to figure out what caused the smell. They retrace Phoenix's steps, and discover lots of different smells in nature - but which one of them is the right match? Tha Phoenix air fàile làidir, neònach fhaighinn,'n dèidh bhith a' cluich còmh' ri Mosaidh, 's chan eil tuigs' aig duine cò às a dh'èirich e. Feumaidh Phoenix snàmh gus cùideas fhaighinn dheth, 's air an slighe chun na h-aibhne, tha na caraidean a' feuchainn ri thuigsinn dè dh'adhbhraich an samh.Gabhaidh 'ad gach ceum a ghabh Phoenix, a' fòghlam iomadh fàile nàdair eadar-dhealaichte... ach cò ac' a tha tighinn a-rèir fàileadh Phoenix?

programme.title: Peicein/Petit
programme.desc: Tha Peicein is Lòra ag argamaid mu dheidhinn cò aca a bu chòir na riaghailtean a dhèanamh suas airson geama Ghriogair is Raghnaill. Fhad ’s a tha iadsan a’ feuchainn ri obrachadh a-mach cò aca a bu chòir a bhith nan sgiobair, tha Griogair agus Raghnall a’ cumail a’ cluich às aonais a’ bhuill. Petit and Laura argue about who should be the one that makes the rules of Greg and Roman's game. While they decide who should be the captain, Greg and Roman wait for them to make a decision and continue playing without the ball.

programme.title: Abadas
programme.desc: Tha thìd ann airson facal Abadas ùr agus turas 'aba-do-be-dee' ùr cuideachd! An-diugh, 's e 'bior-deighe' am facal. Tha na h-Abadas ag ionnsachadh gu bheil ceangal aige ri uisge, ach càite an lorg iad e agus cò bu chòir a dhol ga lorg? It is time for a new Abada word and a new 'aba-do-be-dee' adventure. This time the word is 'icicle'. The Abadas learn that it has something to do with water, but where will they find it and who should go on the adventure?

programme.title: Stòiridh
programme.desc: Sgeulachdan do chlann òga. Tha Kim Carnie a’ leughadh Greta agus na Fuamhairean. Chaidh an leabhar a sgrìobhadh le Zoe Tucker agus a dhealbhachadh le Zoe Persico. Chaidh eadar-theangachadh dhan Ghàidhlig le Mòrag Stiùbhart. A bedtime story for young children. Kim Carnie reads Greta agus na Fuamhairean, written by Zoe Tucker, illustrated by Zoe Persico and translated into Gaelic by Morag Stewart.

programme.title: An Teaghlach Rìoghail an Ath-dhoras/The Royal Next Door
programme.desc: Nuair tha picnic rìoghail dol a ghabhail àite sa phàirc, tha Stella air a dearg nàrachadh, gun fhios nach fhaic a caraidean i an sin. Stella is really embarrassed in case friends see her when she is with her family at a royal picnic in the park.

programme.title: An Teaghlach Rìoghail an Ath-dhoras/The Royal Next Door
programme.desc: Nuair tha Partaidh nam Fiaclairean dol a thachairt, the Mrs Oh 'g iarraidh buidealair. Ach chan eil Mgr P deònach taic a thoirt seachad. Dè nì Stella is an Teaghlach Rìoghail airson cuideachadh leis a’ chuirm? When the Dentist Party is about to take place, Mrs Oh would like a butler. But Mr P isn’t prepared to help out. What will Stella and the Royal Family do to help at the event?

programme.title: Belle and Sebastian
programme.desc: Chan eil riaghailtean a' còrdadh ri Sebastian – ’s tha ’ad sa h-uile h-àit'. Tha e roghainneachadh gum bi e fhèin is Belle nas fheàrr dheth as na beanntan, mar fhiadh-bheanntairean. Ciamar a thèid dhaibh? Rules don't appeal to Sebastian, and they're all around. He decides that he and Belle will be better off in the mountains, like wild mountaineers. How will they get on?

programme.title: Seonaidh | Shaun the Sheep
programme.desc: Tha Bitzer ro dheònach còn na nàire a chuir air agus leigeil leis an treud a h-uile càil a dhèanamh dha. Ach nuair a tha Seonaidh a' mothachadh nach eil cùisean mar bu chòir tha e a' cur roimhe fhèin làmh an uachdair fhaighinn air Bitzer. Bitzer is an all-too-willing volunteer when he has to wear the cone of shame and is happy to let the flock wait on him. Until, that is, Shaun rumbles his malingering and plots the pooch's comeuppance.

programme.title: An Là
programme.desc: Naidheachdan ionadail, nàiseanta is eadar-nàiseanta gach là cuide ri fiosrachadh coimhearsnachd bho BBC ALBA. Local, national and international news and information from BBC ALBA.

programme.title: Brunch le Abigail
programme.desc: Tha an Dutch Baby annasach ach anabarrach blasta. Brunch sònraichte air nach dìochuimhnich thu a’ chiad ghreis. The unusual but extremely delicious Dutch baby is a special brunch that you won't forget in a hurry. In Gaelic with English subtitles.

programme.title: Ball-coise air BBC ALBA/Football on BBC ALBA
programme.desc: An dàrna geam’ eadar Hamilton Academical agus Clyde ann an cuairt dheireannach play-off Lìog a h-Aon beò à Broadwood. Am prògram slàn air BBC ALBA air a’ lìbhrigeadh le Derek MacAoidh agus an sgioba aithris, Ailig O’Henley agus Stephen Craigan. The second leg of the League One play-off final between Hamilton Academical and Clyde from Broadwood. Full match coverage with presenter Derek MacKay and the commentary team of Alex O’Henley and Stephen Craigan.

programme.title: Famous Five
programme.desc: An sgeulachd iongantach aig Smith, Johnstone, Reilly, Turnbull agus Ormond; an loidhne-aghaidh iomraiteach no am "Famous Five" aig Hibernian FC a chuir ball-coise na h-Alba fon casan sna bliadhnaichean as dèidh an dara cogaidh. The remarkable story of Smith, Johnstone, Reilly, Turnbull and Ormond, Hibernian FC's talented 'Famous Five' forward line, which dominated Scottish football in the post-war period.

programme.title: Belladrum
programme.desc: Tha Fiona NicChoinnich is Niall Iain Dòmhnallach a’ lìbhrigeadh seisean acoustic bho rionnag ùr, Michael Lewis, aig Belladrum 2025. Fo bhuaidh Frank Sinatra, tha an deugaire na sheinneadair ceòl jazz is swing à Baile Ùr an t-Slèibhe is air inbhe a choisinn an dèidh àite fhaighinn aig Taigh-òsta Grand Galvez ann an Texas mar neach-ciùil air mhuinntireas – a’ leantainn ann an ceumannan iodhal-ciùil. Fiona MacKenzie and Niall Iain Macdonald present an acoustic session from rising star Michael Lewis at Belladrum. Inspired by Frank Sinatra, the teenage jazz and swing singer from Newtonmore has rapidly risen to prominence, having landed a prestigious musical residency at the Grand Galvez Hotel in Texas, following in the footsteps of his idol.

programme.title: Seirm
programme.desc: Prògram de cheòl traidiseanta agus freumhach air a lìbhrigeadh le Màiri Anna NicUalraig. Air fhilmeadh aig àm Celtic Connections 2025 agus a’ taisbeanaidh chlàraidhean is chòmhraidhean a chaidh a dhèanamh a dh’aona ghothach airson Seirm, chìte cuid den luchd-ciùil a b’ fheàrr a bha aig an fhèis, leithid Ímar, Larry Campbell & Teresa Williams, The East Pointers, Georgia Cécile agus Ainsley Hamill. Traditional and roots music show presented by Mary Ann Kennedy. Filmed during Celtic Connections 2025, Seirm showcases bespoke recordings and conversations with some of the best artists appearing at the festival. This episode features performances from Ímar, Larry Campbell and Teresa Williams, The East Pointers, Georgia Cécile and Ainsley Hamill. In Gaelic with English subtitles.

programme.title: Bob Marley Reimagined
programme.desc: Celebrate the rich legacy of reggae legend Bob Marley in a concert filmed live at Birmingham Town Hall, featuring some of his most celebrated songs and special guests including his grandson Skip Marley. Presented by Trevor Nelson, this one-hour special reimagines Bob Marley’s greatest hits, including Get Up Stand Up, Exodus, Redemption Song and Waiting in Vain, all layered with new orchestration by Chineke!, Europe’s first majority black and ethnically diverse orchestra. Chineke! are joined by singer-songwriter JP Cooper, gospel and R&B legend Ruby Turner and Skip Marley, who makes his debut UK solo performance. Featuring interviews with the performers and members of the Marley family, this concert both honours and brings fresh interpretation to the beloved music of Bob Marley.

programme.title: The Media Show
programme.desc: Twenty years ago a man arriving for a job interview at BBC Television Centre was taken into a live TV studio and asked to comment on a legal story. The clip quickly spread on early video-sharing sites and became a meme. Guy Goma reflects on what happened, alongside Elliott Gotkine, the journalist involved in the original error. Saudi Arabia has spent large sums on sport and media in recent years, aiming to build influence as well as make financial returns. New developments, including changes to sports funding and involvement in major media deals, suggest a shift in approach. Claire Enders, founder of Enders Analysis, and Claire Atkinson, contributing editor at The Ankler and founder of Media Mix, outline how the strategy is changing. Climate change remains one of the most complex stories for news organisations to cover. It involves long-term change, scientific detail and questions about how to keep audiences engaged. David Shukman, journalist and former BBC Science Editor, sets out his view on how climate reporting has developed and the issues it faces.

programme.title: Rip Off Britain
programme.desc: Gloria Hunniford, Julia Somerville and Louise Minchin investigate how a scammer was able to cancel one man’s flight when he believed he was receiving customer support from the airline on social media. The team reveals which airlines’ security processes allow flights to be cancelled with only minimal details provided. Also on the programme, the coeliac cruise passenger who was told all the food on board was cooked using an ingredient she was allergic to. And at the advice clinic in South Shields, a woman who had to endure a revolting holiday cottage stay. Why wasn’t she offered compensation?

programme.title: Homes Under the Hammer
programme.desc: A former care centre in Waterlooville is converted into a smart family home for a young couple, their baby daughter, ten pet dogs and their dog grooming business. Developers in West Bromwich sort out a house with subsidence, and in Birkenhead a developer gives a refurbished semi-detached to his daughter as a birthday present.

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: Roo Irvine takes to the streets to quiz the good folk of Leominster in Herefordshire about her mystery object. Encased in brass with a screw top at one end, what is it? Across town, two teams are puzzling over what to buy with their budgets of £300. Guiding the red team is Charles Hanson. Friends Toni and Debbie reckon they know how to get their way when it comes to bagging a bargain. Let’s see if they can out-haggle the blue team, friends and company bosses Russ and Jay. With antiques expert Richard Madley by their side, the blues tune into a Bakelite radio – but are they on the same wavelength when it comes to the price? Meanwhile, the reds consider pouring their money into a rustic jug – until they see the price tag. Can they exterminate the competition with a vintage Dalek toy instead? With their shopping bags full, the teams cross the border into north Wales to sell their items at Matthew Tong’s auction. Which team is his money on?

programme.title: Celebrity Escape to the Country
programme.desc: The spotlight is on actor, singer and West End and Broadway star Alfie Boe, who is swapping the West End stage for some house-hunting in Sussex. Ginny Buckley presents him with a selection of show-stopping rural properties, and in between touring bricks, mortar and weather boarding, the duo take a break to race agricultural vehicles at a vintage tractor club. programme.title: The Repair Shop on the Road
programme.desc: The team help a charity get their iconic bus back on the road, Mark Stuckey reaches for the stars, fixing an unusual projector, and Will is wowed by the lost art of encaustic tiles.

programme.title: Bridge of Lies
programme.desc: Ross Kemp has his hands full as he presents a special edition of the nail-biting quiz in which a team of celebrity drag queens, featuring The Vivienne, Tia Kofi, Kitty Scott-Claus and Lawrence Chaney, get together to take on the Bridge of Lies for their chosen charity. One by one, they all face the Bridge, choosing who faces each crossing depending on the question category. Each Bridge crossing has 32 potential steps, including 22 truths and ten lies. They must cross the Bridge by stepping on the truths and avoiding the lies, earning money for each correct answer. Step on a lie, and the Bridge will halve their money. Step on three lies, and they are out of the game. There is always a safe path across the Bridge. They just have to find it. Once they have each faced the Bridge on their own, those who have been successful will join forces to face the final crossing for a chance to take home the cash.

programme.title: Panorama
programme.desc: Cute, funny, and sometimes surreal, AI-generated videos are flooding our social media feeds, but behind the dancing dogs and talking fruit lies a far darker world. In this Panorama investigation, reporter Marianna Spring explores how AI slop is shaping what we see, what we believe and who we can trust. From scam adverts and cloned voices to deepfake fraud, political manipulation and racially charged disinformation, the programme reveals how cheap and easily available AI tools are being weaponised. We ask, in the age of artificial intelligence, will seeing ever be believing again?

programme.title: Bargain Hunt

Friends Toni and Debbie reckon they know how to get their way when it comes to bagging a bargain. Let’s see if they can out-haggle the blue team, friends and company bosses Russ and Jay. Meanwhile, the reds consider pouring their money into a rustic jug – until they see the price tag. Can they exterminate the competition with a vintage Dalek toy instead? With their shopping bags full, the teams cross the border into north Wales to sell their items at Matthew Tong’s auction. Which team is his money on?

programme.title: Bridge of Lies
programme.desc: Ross Kemp has his hands full as he presents a special edition of the nail-biting quiz in which a team of celebrity drag queens, featuring The Vivienne, Tia Kofi, Kitty Scott-Claus and Lawrence Chaney, get together to take on the Bridge of Lies for their chosen charity. One by one, they all face the Bridge, choosing who faces each crossing depending on the question category. Each Bridge crossing has 32 potential steps, including 22 truths and ten lies. They must cross the Bridge by stepping on the truths and avoiding the lies, earning money for each correct answer. Step on a lie, and the Bridge will halve their money. Step on three lies, and they are out of the game. There is always a safe path across the Bridge. They just have to find it. Once they have each faced the Bridge on their own, those who have been successful will join forces to face the final crossing for a chance to take home the cash.

programme.title: Panorama
programme.desc: Cute, funny, and sometimes surreal, AI-generated videos are flooding our social media feeds, but behind the dancing dogs and talking fruit lies a far darker world. In this Panorama investigation, reporter Marianna Spring explores how AI slop is shaping what we see, what we believe and who we can trust. From scam adverts and cloned voices to deepfake fraud, political manipulation and racially charged disinformation, the programme reveals how cheap and easily available AI tools are being weaponised. We ask, in the age of artificial intelligence, will seeing ever be believing again?

programme.title: Panorama
programme.desc: Cute, funny, and sometimes surreal, AI-generated videos are flooding our social media feeds, but behind the dancing dogs and talking fruit lies a far darker world. In this Panorama investigation, reporter Marianna Spring explores how AI slop is shaping what we see, what we believe and who we can trust. From scam adverts and cloned voices to deepfake fraud, political manipulation and racially charged disinformation, the programme reveals how cheap and easily available AI tools are being weaponised. We ask, in the age of artificial intelligence, will seeing ever be believing again?

programme.title: Rip Off Britain
programme.desc: Gloria Hunniford, Julia Somerville and Louise Minchin investigate how a scammer was able to cancel one man’s flight when he believed he was receiving customer support from the airline on social media. The team reveals which airlines’ security processes allow flights to be cancelled with only minimal details provided. Also on the programme, the coeliac cruise passenger who was told all the food on board was cooked using an ingredient she was allergic to. And at the advice clinic in South Shields, a woman who had to endure a revolting holiday cottage stay. Why wasn’t she offered compensation?

programme.title: Homes Under the Hammer
programme.desc: A former care centre in Waterlooville is converted into a smart family home for a young couple, their baby daughter, ten pet dogs and their dog grooming business. Developers in West Bromwich sort out a house with subsidence, and in Birkenhead a developer gives a refurbished semi-detached to his daughter as a birthday present.

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: Roo Irvine takes to the streets to quiz the good folk of Leominster in Herefordshire about her mystery object. Encased in brass with a screw top at one end, what is it? Across town, two teams are puzzling over what to buy with their budgets of £300. Guiding the red team is Charles Hanson. Friends Toni and Debbie reckon they know how to get their way when it comes to bagging a bargain. Let’s see if they can out-haggle the blue team, friends and company bosses Russ and Jay. With antiques expert Richard Madley by their side, the blues tune into a Bakelite radio – but are they on the same wavelength when it comes to the price? Meanwhile, the reds consider pouring their money into a rustic jug – until they see the price tag. Can they exterminate the competition with a vintage Dalek toy instead? With their shopping bags full, the teams cross the border into north Wales to sell their items at Matthew Tong’s auction. Which team is his money on?

programme.title: BBC News at One
programme.desc: The latest national and international news from the BBC.

programme.title: Father Brown
programme.desc: Sullivan’s dream of leaving Kembleford is scuppered when he is arrested for receiving stolen goods.

programme.title: Celebrity Escape to the Country
programme.desc: The spotlight is on actor, singer and West End and Broadway star Alfie Boe, who is swapping the West End stage for some house-hunting in Sussex. Ginny Buckley presents him with a selection of show-stopping rural properties, and in between touring bricks, mortar and weather boarding, the duo take a break to race agricultural vehicles at a vintage tractor club. Can Alfie find his dream home and keep up with Ginny on the track?

programme.title: The Repair Shop on the Road
programme.desc: The team help a charity get their iconic bus back on the road, Mark Stuckey reaches for the stars, fixing an unusual projector, and Will is wowed by the lost art of encaustic tiles.

programme.title: Bridge of Lies
programme.desc: Ross Kemp has his hands full as he presents a special edition of the nail-biting quiz in which a team of celebrity drag queens, featuring The Vivienne, Tia Kofi, Kitty Scott-Claus and Lawrence Chaney, get together to take on the Bridge of Lies for their chosen charity. One by one, they all face the Bridge, choosing who faces each crossing depending on the question category. Each Bridge crossing has 32 potential steps, including 22 truths and ten lies. They must cross the Bridge by stepping on the truths and avoiding the lies, earning money for each correct answer. Step on a lie, and the Bridge will halve their money. Step on three lies, and they are out of the game. There is always a safe path across the Bridge. They just have to find it. Once they have each faced the Bridge on their own, those who have been successful will join forces to face the final crossing for a chance to take home the cash.

programme.desc: Gloria Hunniford, Julia Somerville and Louise Minchin investigate how a scammer was able to cancel one man’s flight when he believed he was receiving customer support from the airline on social media. The team reveals which airlines’ security processes allow flights to be cancelled with only minimal details provided. Also on the programme, the coeliac cruise passenger who was told all the food on board was cooked using an ingredient she was allergic to. And at the advice clinic in South Shields, a woman who had to endure a revolting holiday cottage stay. Why wasn’t she offered compensation?

programme.title: Homes Under the Hammer
programme.desc: A former care centre in Waterlooville is converted into a smart family home for a young couple, their baby daughter, ten pet dogs and their dog grooming business. Developers in West Bromwich sort out a house with subsidence, and in Birkenhead a developer gives a refurbished semi-detached to his daughter as a birthday present.

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: Roo Irvine takes to the streets to quiz the good folk of Leominster in Herefordshire about her mystery object. Encased in brass with a screw top at one end, what is it? Across town, two teams are puzzling over what to buy with their budgets of £300. Guiding the red team is Charles Hanson. Friends Toni and Debbie reckon they know how to get their way when it comes to bagging a bargain. Let’s see if they can out-haggle the blue team, friends and company bosses Russ and Jay. With antiques expert Richard Madley by their side, the blues tune into a Bakelite radio – but are they on the same wavelength when it comes to the price? Meanwhile, the reds consider pouring their money into a rustic jug – until they see the price tag. Can they exterminate the competition with a vintage Dalek toy instead? With their shopping bags full, the teams cross the border into north Wales to sell their items at Matthew Tong’s auction. Which team is his money on?

programme.desc: The spotlight is on actor, singer and West End and Broadway star Alfie Boe, who is swapping the West End stage for some house-hunting in Sussex. Ginny Buckley presents him with a selection of show-stopping rural properties, and in between touring bricks, mortar and weather boarding, the duo take a break to race agricultural vehicles at a vintage tractor club. programme.title: The Repair Shop on the Road

programme.title: Bridge of Lies
programme.desc: Ross Kemp has his hands full as he presents a special edition of the nail-biting quiz in which a team of celebrity drag queens, featuring The Vivienne, Tia Kofi, Kitty Scott-Claus and Lawrence Chaney, get together to take on the Bridge of Lies for their chosen charity. One by one, they all face the Bridge, choosing who faces each crossing depending on the question category. Each Bridge crossing has 32 potential steps, including 22 truths and ten lies. They must cross the Bridge by stepping on the truths and avoiding the lies, earning money for each correct answer. Step on a lie, and the Bridge will halve their money. Step on three lies, and they are out of the game. There is always a safe path across the Bridge. They just have to find it. Once they have each faced the Bridge on their own, those who have been successful will join forces to face the final crossing for a chance to take home the cash.

programme.title: Bridge of Lies
programme.desc: Ross Kemp has his hands full as he presents a special edition of the nail-biting quiz in which a team of celebrity drag queens, featuring The Vivienne, Tia Kofi, Kitty Scott-Claus and Lawrence Chaney, get together to take on the Bridge of Lies for their chosen charity. One by one, they all face the Bridge, choosing who faces each crossing depending on the question category. Each Bridge crossing has 32 potential steps, including 22 truths and ten lies. They must cross the Bridge by stepping on the truths and avoiding the lies, earning money for each correct answer. Step on a lie, and the Bridge will halve their money. Step on three lies, and they are out of the game. There is always a safe path across the Bridge. They just have to find it. Once they have each faced the Bridge on their own, those who have been successful will join forces to face the final crossing for a chance to take home the cash.

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: Roo Irvine takes to the streets to quiz the good folk of Leominster in Herefordshire about her mystery object. Encased in brass with a screw top at one end, what is it? Across town, two teams are puzzling over what to buy with their budgets of £300. Guiding the red team is Charles Hanson. Friends Toni and Debbie reckon they know how to get their way when it comes to bagging a bargain. Let’s see if they can out-haggle the blue team, friends and company bosses Russ and Jay. With antiques expert Richard Madley by their side, the blues tune into a Bakelite radio – but are they on the same wavelength when it comes to the price? Meanwhile, the reds consider pouring their money into a rustic jug – until they see the price tag. Can they exterminate the competition with a vintage Dalek toy instead? With their shopping bags full, the teams cross the border into north Wales to sell their items at Matthew Tong’s auction. Which team is his money on?

programme.title: Panorama
programme.desc: Cute, funny, and sometimes surreal, AI-generated videos are flooding our social media feeds, but behind the dancing dogs and talking fruit lies a far darker world. In this Panorama investigation, reporter Marianna Spring explores how AI slop is shaping what we see, what we believe and who we can trust. From scam adverts and cloned voices to deepfake fraud, political manipulation and racially charged disinformation, the programme reveals how cheap and easily available AI tools are being weaponised. We ask, in the age of artificial intelligence, will seeing ever be believing again?

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: Roo Irvine takes to the streets to quiz the good folk of Leominster in Herefordshire about her mystery object. Encased in brass with a screw top at one end, what is it? Across town, two teams are puzzling over what to buy with their budgets of £300. Guiding the red team is Charles Hanson. Friends Toni and Debbie reckon they know how to get their way when it comes to bagging a bargain. Let’s see if they can out-haggle the blue team, friends and company bosses Russ and Jay. With antiques expert Richard Madley by their side, the blues tune into a Bakelite radio – but are they on the same wavelength when it comes to the price? Meanwhile, the reds consider pouring their money into a rustic jug – until they see the price tag. Can they exterminate the competition with a vintage Dalek toy instead? With their shopping bags full, the teams cross the border into north Wales to sell their items at Matthew Tong’s auction. Which team is his money on?

programme.title: Bridge of Lies
programme.desc: Ross Kemp has his hands full as he presents a special edition of the nail-biting quiz in which a team of celebrity drag queens, featuring The Vivienne, Tia Kofi, Kitty Scott-Claus and Lawrence Chaney, get together to take on the Bridge of Lies for their chosen charity. One by one, they all face the Bridge, choosing who faces each crossing depending on the question category. Each Bridge crossing has 32 potential steps, including 22 truths and ten lies. They must cross the Bridge by stepping on the truths and avoiding the lies, earning money for each correct answer. Step on a lie, and the Bridge will halve their money. Step on three lies, and they are out of the game. There is always a safe path across the Bridge. They just have to find it. Once they have each faced the Bridge on their own, those who have been successful will join forces to face the final crossing for a chance to take home the cash.

programme.title: Panorama
programme.desc: Cute, funny, and sometimes surreal, AI-generated videos are flooding our social media feeds, but behind the dancing dogs and talking fruit lies a far darker world. In this Panorama investigation, reporter Marianna Spring explores how AI slop is shaping what we see, what we believe and who we can trust. From scam adverts and cloned voices to deepfake fraud, political manipulation and racially charged disinformation, the programme reveals how cheap and easily available AI tools are being weaponised. We ask, in the age of artificial intelligence, will seeing ever be believing again?

programme.title: Father Brown

programme.title: Celebrity Escape to the Country
programme.desc: The spotlight is on actor, singer and West End and Broadway star Alfie Boe, who is swapping the West End stage for some house-hunting in Sussex. Ginny Buckley presents him with a selection of show-stopping rural properties, and in between touring bricks, mortar and weather boarding, the duo take a break to race agricultural vehicles at a vintage tractor club. Can Alfie find his dream home and keep up with Ginny on the track?

programme.title: The Repair Shop on the Road
programme.desc: The team help a charity get their iconic bus back on the road, Mark Stuckey reaches for the stars, fixing an unusual projector, and Will is wowed by the lost art of encaustic tiles.

programme.title: Bridge of Lies
programme.desc: Ross Kemp has his hands full as he presents a special edition of the nail-biting quiz in which a team of celebrity drag queens, featuring The Vivienne, Tia Kofi, Kitty Scott-Claus and Lawrence Chaney, get together to take on the Bridge of Lies for their chosen charity. One by one, they all face the Bridge, choosing who faces each crossing depending on the question category. Each Bridge crossing has 32 potential steps, including 22 truths and ten lies. They must cross the Bridge by stepping on the truths and avoiding the lies, earning money for each correct answer. Step on a lie, and the Bridge will halve their money. Step on three lies, and they are out of the game. There is always a safe path across the Bridge. They just have to find it. Once they have each faced the Bridge on their own, those who have been successful will join forces to face the final crossing for a chance to take home the cash.

programme.title: Pointless
programme.desc: Alexander Armstrong is joined by co-host Susan Wokoma for the brainy quiz where the contestants try to score as few points as possible by plumbing the depths of their general knowledge to come up with the answers no-one else could think of.

programme.title: 21st Century TV with Lucy Owen
programme.desc: Lucy invites viewers to relive the highlights and stories that shaped Wales in 2005. There is sporting success in rugby and netball, Donny Osmond is in Merthyr, and a rare spider is found. Homes in a Welsh valley are finally plugged into the grid while Carmarthen Etta bakes a royal wedding cake. There’s a controversial art installation, the oldest car in Wales goes up for auction and Catrin Finch reinvents harp playing for the next generation.

programme.title: Breakfast
programme.desc: The latest news, sport, business and weather from the BBC's Breakfast team.

programme.title: Morning Live
programme.desc: Morning Live is BBC One’s flagship daytime programme, bringing you the best advice from familiar faces across the BBC, original journalism and investigations, and a sparkle of Strictly magic

programme.title: Rip Off Britain
programme.desc: Gloria Hunniford, Julia Somerville and Louise Minchin investigate how a scammer was able to cancel one man’s flight when he believed he was receiving customer support from the airline on social media. The team reveals which airlines’ security processes allow flights to be cancelled with only minimal details provided. Also on the programme, the coeliac cruise passenger who was told all the food on board was cooked using an ingredient she was allergic to. And at the advice clinic in South Shields, a woman who had to endure a revolting holiday cottage stay. Why wasn’t she offered compensation?

programme.title: Homes Under the Hammer
programme.desc: A former care centre in Waterlooville is converted into a smart family home for a young couple, their baby daughter, ten pet dogs and their dog grooming business. Developers in West Bromwich sort out a house with subsidence, and in Birkenhead a developer gives a refurbished semi-detached to his daughter as a birthday present.

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: Roo Irvine takes to the streets to quiz the good folk of Leominster in Herefordshire about her mystery object. Encased in brass with a screw top at one end, what is it? Across town, two teams are puzzling over what to buy with their budgets of £300. Guiding the red team is Charles Hanson. Friends Toni and Debbie reckon they know how to get their way when it comes to bagging a bargain. Let’s see if they can out-haggle the blue team, friends and company bosses Russ and Jay. With antiques expert Richard Madley by their side, the blues tune into a Bakelite radio – but are they on the same wavelength when it comes to the price? Meanwhile, the reds consider pouring their money into a rustic jug – until they see the price tag. Can they exterminate the competition with a vintage Dalek toy instead? With their shopping bags full, the teams cross the border into north Wales to sell their items at Matthew Tong’s auction. Which team is his money on?

programme.title: Panorama
programme.desc: Cute, funny, and sometimes surreal, AI-generated videos are flooding our social media feeds, but behind the dancing dogs and talking fruit lies a far darker world. In this Panorama investigation, reporter Marianna Spring explores how AI slop is shaping what we see, what we believe and who we can trust. From scam adverts and cloned voices to deepfake fraud, political manipulation and racially charged disinformation, the programme reveals how cheap and easily available AI tools are being weaponised. We ask, in the age of artificial intelligence, will seeing ever be believing again?

programme.title: Homes Under the Hammer
programme.desc: A former care centre in Waterlooville is converted into a smart family home for a young couple, their baby daughter, ten pet dogs and their dog grooming business. programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: Roo Irvine takes to the streets to quiz the good folk of Leominster in Herefordshire about her mystery object. Encased in brass with a screw top at one end, what is it? Across town, two teams are puzzling over what to buy with their budgets of £300. Guiding the red team is Charles Hanson. Friends Toni and Debbie reckon they know how to get their way when it comes to bagging a bargain. Let’s see if they can out-haggle the blue team, friends and company bosses Russ and Jay. With antiques expert Richard Madley by their side, the blues tune into a Bakelite radio – but are they on the same wavelength when it comes to the price? Meanwhile, the reds consider pouring their money into a rustic jug – until they see the price tag. Can they exterminate the competition with a vintage Dalek toy instead? programme.title: The Repair Shop on the Road

programme.title: Bridge of Lies
programme.desc: Ross Kemp has his hands full as he presents a special edition of the nail-biting quiz in which a team of celebrity drag queens, featuring The Vivienne, Tia Kofi, Kitty Scott-Claus and Lawrence Chaney, get together to take on the Bridge of Lies for their chosen charity. One by one, they all face the Bridge, choosing who faces each crossing depending on the question category. Each Bridge crossing has 32 potential steps, including 22 truths and ten lies. They must cross the Bridge by stepping on the truths and avoiding the lies, earning money for each correct answer. Step on a lie, and the Bridge will halve their money. Step on three lies, and they are out of the game. There is always a safe path across the Bridge. They just have to find it. Once they have each faced the Bridge on their own, those who have been successful will join forces to face the final crossing for a chance to take home the cash.

programme.desc: Roo Irvine takes to the streets to quiz the good folk of Leominster in Herefordshire about her mystery object. Encased in brass with a screw top at one end, what is it? Across town, two teams are puzzling over what to buy with their budgets of £300. Guiding the red team is Charles Hanson. Friends Toni and Debbie reckon they know how to get their way when it comes to bagging a bargain. Let’s see if they can out-haggle the blue team, friends and company bosses Russ and Jay. With antiques expert Richard Madley by their side, the blues tune into a Bakelite radio – but are they on the same wavelength when it comes to the price? Meanwhile, the reds consider pouring their money into a rustic jug – until they see the price tag. Can they exterminate the competition with a vintage Dalek toy instead? With their shopping bags full, the teams cross the border into north Wales to sell their items at Matthew Tong’s auction. Which team is his money on?

programme.title: Celebrity Escape to the Country

Ginny Buckley presents him with a selection of show-stopping rural properties, and in between touring bricks, mortar and weather boarding, the duo take a break to race agricultural vehicles at a vintage tractor club. programme.title: Bridge of Lies
programme.desc: Ross Kemp has his hands full as he presents a special edition of the nail-biting quiz in which a team of celebrity drag queens, featuring The Vivienne, Tia Kofi, Kitty Scott-Claus and Lawrence Chaney, get together to take on the Bridge of Lies for their chosen charity. One by one, they all face the Bridge, choosing who faces each crossing depending on the question category. Each Bridge crossing has 32 potential steps, including 22 truths and ten lies. They must cross the Bridge by stepping on the truths and avoiding the lies, earning money for each correct answer. Step on a lie, and the Bridge will halve their money. Step on three lies, and they are out of the game. There is always a safe path across the Bridge. They just have to find it. Once they have each faced the Bridge on their own, those who have been successful will join forces to face the final crossing for a chance to take home the cash.

programme.title: Panorama
programme.desc: Cute, funny, and sometimes surreal, AI-generated videos are flooding our social media feeds, but behind the dancing dogs and talking fruit lies a far darker world. In this Panorama investigation, reporter Marianna Spring explores how AI slop is shaping what we see, what we believe and who we can trust. From scam adverts and cloned voices to deepfake fraud, political manipulation and racially charged disinformation, the programme reveals how cheap and easily available AI tools are being weaponised. We ask, in the age of artificial intelligence, will seeing ever be believing again?

programme.desc: 1993. Niall is conflicted when asked by his mother to lie in court about Ruben’s violence. Ruben seems to have changed for the better, so the decision weighs heavily on him.

programme.title: Two Doors Down
programme.desc: Beth and Eric think Ian is taking them out for their 30th wedding anniversary dinner but find instead that he and Gordon have organised a surprise party at their house. And the gang is all there. What more could you ask from a party? The buffet table is groaning with food, the champagne is flowing and Christine has brought a homemade trifle as a present. There is a wander down memory lane, a look at the Bairds' wedding album and an illuminating quiz. Ian tries to keep the focus on the anniversary couple but a drunken Cathy tries to prompt wedding proposals from reluctant boyfriends Ian and Alan, and treats Eric, Beth and the rest of the guests to a replay of her and Colin's first wedding dance.

programme.title: Loop
programme.desc: Josie KO’s sculptures emit a burst of colour and mischief, but beneath the gaudy knitted skirts and over-the-top wigs lies a more serious message. After reading Scottish poet William Dunbar’s poem Of Ane Blak-Moir, one of the first recorded documents of the presence of black people in Scotland, Josie took the racist caricatures of the poem and turned them on their head, using DIY and papier maché to create figures that are difficult to ignore.

programme.title: A Good Girl's Guide to Murder
programme.desc: It’s the summer holidays, but teenager Pip is focused on her school research project investigating the case of 17-year-old Andie Bell, whose disappearance in 2019 has haunted the town of Little Kilton. Andie’s boyfriend Sal Singh sent a text confessing to the murder before being found dead, seemingly taking his own life. Andie’s body was never found. With her own secret connection to what happened five years ago, Pip is determined to prove Sal’s innocence.

programme.title: A Good Girl's Guide to Murder
programme.desc: Now a team, Pip and Ravi turn their attention to Andie’s best friends and find out Andie had a secret life that Sal was unhappy about. Meanwhile, Pip receives an anonymous warning.

Ravi is sceptical about Pip’s plan, but she’s determined to see it through and attend the party with Cara and Lauren.

programme.desc: The eight remaining designers pair up to create uplifting spaces for a homelessness charity in London. They tackle an arts and crafts room, a group workshop room, a wellness area and an employment suite. The charity’s ambassador, Dara Ó Briain, joins Alan to check in on the designers before Michelle and guest judge Sophie Robinson critique the spaces.

programme.title: The Cage
programme.desc: Matty flails as Ning continues to push him. Meanwhile, Leanne and Gary bond, until he pressures Leanne to betray Matty to safeguard her family.

programme.title: This is BBC Two
programme.desc: Highlights of programmes on BBC Two.

programme.title: Escape to the Country
programme.desc: Nicki Chapman is in stunning south west Wales, helping Carol, along with her husband, return to the country where she grew up. With her son Greg supporting her on the house hunt, she’s dreaming of a home close to the sea. The property line-up includes a picture-perfect double-fronted house with roses around the door, and a mystery house boasting spectacular mountain views... it’s Wales at its most wonderful.

programme.title: Great Central Asian Railway Journeys
programme.desc: Michael Portillo’s railway tour through Uzbekistan continues in the lush oasis surrounding the historic city of Samarkand. Here, he uncovers the Central Asian origins of the apple, a fruit that travelled to Europe along the Silk Road. Exploring vast orchards, he witnesses how millions of apples are grown and processed here each year. Boarding a high-speed train along the old Trans-Caspian Railway, Michael hears how the Russians toiled to build this remarkable line through the shifting sands of Uzbekistan’s steppe. In Bukhara, he explores the faded magnificence of an abandoned Russian imperial palace. He then enters the city’s Islamic heart, and standing in the shadow of the Ark, the city's striking fortified citadel, he unearths the deadly intrigue between Britain and Russia in what became known as the Great Game - and discovers the fate of two British officers thrown into the infamous 'bug pit'.

programme.title: Just One Thing
programme.desc: Clive Myrie is in Kent with Tracey, a soon-to-be grandmother who is worried about her high blood pressure. His suggestion? Borrow a pet – yes, really. With new apps making it simple to match people with animals, Tracey could enjoy all the benefits without the long-term commitment. And the science is clear: spending time with animals boosts happiness, improves wellbeing and lowers the risk of dying from cardiovascular disease. A furry friend might be just what her heart needs.

programme.title: Ronan Keating's Wild Atlantic
programme.desc: Ronan completes this leg of his journey along Ireland's Wild Atlantic in County Derry/Londonderry. He walks the 400-year-old walls of the city with comedian Diona Doherty, and hits the farm to find out just what it takes to be a competitive sheep herder, before heading for the windswept coastline of Castlerock to meet a skilled craft worker who builds traditional coracle boats by hand.

programme.title: BBC News
programme.desc: Twenty-four hours a day, the latest national and international stories as they break.

programme.title: Political Thinking with Nick Robinson
programme.desc: Miatta Fahnbulleh, the first minister to walk out of Keir Starmer’s government since the May elections, talks about mistakes in Downing Street, the PM’s leadership and why she is backing Andy Burnham.

programme.title: Impossible
programme.desc: Game show in which 24 players compete across the series, scoring points by answering questions correctly. However, they must avoid the impossible answers, otherwise they will be eliminated from the show until the next day. In each episode there are three rounds, and the three highest scorers from each round play against each other in the final. The winner of this battle faces a £10,000 question.

programme.title: Mastermind
programme.desc: The hunt for the nation's Mastermind continues as Clive Myrie tests four more contenders on their specialist subjects and general knowledge. The specialist subjects are Marie Curie, the BBC sitcom Ghosts, Elizabeth Woodville and Banksy.

programme.title: Lightning
programme.desc: Comedian Zoe Lyons presents the electrifyingly fast quiz with a £3,000 jackpot. Six plucky contestants compete across six rounds testing their general knowledge, quick thinking and speedy reactions whilst our ruthless spotlight patrols the studio. The contestants’ motivation in each round is simple: stay out of the light and you’ll be alright!

programme.title: Clean It, Fix It
programme.desc: Olivia lives in a one-bedroom flat in London, where every inch of floor space counts, so the team turn her tired and unloved courtyard into an extra living space with some clever storage solutions.

programme.title: Super Smart Animals
programme.desc: For centuries, the idea of intelligent animals struck most people as ridiculous. But not any more - the latest science reveals that animals are a lot smarter than we thought. In the second of two programmes, Liz Bonnin embarks on a worldwide search for the planet's most intelligent animals. Liz meets grey whales with emotions much like our own, unravels how the Caribbean's cleverest monkeys outwit their human neighbours, and even has a conversation with the world's cleverest chimp - with some surprising consequences. Explore how Seattle's crows can hold grudges for years, discover that the cleverest dogs can learn over 1,000 words, and find out why Asian elephants can spend hours looking at themselves in giant mirrors. Then there is meerkat school, eye-poking capuchin armies, and even a new version of Einstein's infamous equation written by a sheepdog. Prepare to be amazed, entertained, and even outwitted by the world's Super Smart Animals.

programme.title: Antiques Roadshow
programme.desc: Michael Aspel invites members of the public to bring along their antiques for examination. The team travel to the northernmost point of Great Britain to visit Shetland. Among the objects that turn up are a valuable enamelled 18th century glass, a painting of a local man by the celebrated railway artist Terence Cuneo, a rare 18th century Chinese 'Ho' pot and a Scottish pearl set in a gold ring.

programme.title: Flog It!
programme.desc: This episode comes from Tilbury Docks in Essex, where antiques experts Elizabeth Talbot and Philip Serrell search for items to take off to auction. Elizabeth finds a mint toy car collection, and Philip unearths a trench periscope from the First World War. Paul Martin uncovers the explosive history of Britain’s biggest gunpowder factory.

programme.title: Richard Osman's House of Games
programme.desc: Every day this week, celebrity contestants Deirdre O'Kane, Jay Rayner, Tessa Sanderson and Iwan Thomas take on a series of quiz rounds selected by the host, quiz legend Richard Osman. A daily winner is declared following a quickfire round at the end of each show, and the scores are tallied across the week, resulting in an overall champion being crowned on Friday. Will the winning stars opt for the much-coveted House of Games decanter, or will they be tempted by the House of Games retro bag?

programme.title: Great Central Asian Railway Journeys
programme.desc: Michael Portillo’s railway adventure through Uzbekistan reaches its finale in the historic city of Bukhara. Amidst the medieval Islamic architecture, Michael goes in search of a centuries-old Jewish community. Stepping inside a 420-year-old synagogue and a family home, he’s introduced to unique customs and traditions, and a fragrant green dish that has made Bukharan Jews famous worldwide. Michael grapples with kurash, an ancient form of upright wrestling once used to select the bravest warriors and now also increasingly popular as a sport for young Uzbek women. Michael’s exploration of Uzbekistan culminates in the vast Kyzylkum Desert, where he experiences the life of nomadic tribes who once roamed its vast sandy plains. His Central Asian journey concludes among the horses and riders who brave all to take part in one of the most dangerous equestrian sports in the world.

programme.title: Greatest Gardens with Diarmuid Gavin and Carol Klein
programme.desc: Carol Klein and Diarmuid Gavin lead the search along with guest judge and keen gardener Katie Piper to find Northern Ireland’s greatest garden. Up first is Colin’s surprising suburban rustic garden in suburban Ballymena. In the foothills of the Sperrin Mountains, near the windswept Glenshane Pass, Adrienne has transformed two acres using a variety of planting styles. The final stop is in Dromore, where Julietta has created a garden designed with her young family very much in mind, including a wild meadow playground and a courtyard filled with edible plants. There are mixed opinions at the judging table – so which will expert judges Diarmuid, Carol and Katie feel deserves a place in the Greatest Garden final?

programme.title: Beechgrove Garden
programme.desc: It's time for some early summer colour as Carole Baxter makes the first of her visits to classic Scottish gardens. She visits Glenarn, which has a fabulous collection of rhododendrons looking their best right now. Back at Beechgrove Garden, George Anderson and Calum Clunie are busy refreshing the grass and gravel plot and planting new varieties. Calum demonstrates how to take cuttings from a fuchsia, and there are some ideas on how to manage your plot if you are unlucky enough to have club root in your vegetable patch. And there are all the usual handy hints.

programme.title: Gardeners' World
programme.desc: With the promise of warmer days ahead, Monty makes a start on planting up some of his spectacular summer containers. He’s also got leeks to plant out and shares some advice on how to make your own fertiliser. Frances Tophill heads to Berkshire to learn more about biodynamic gardening and the benefits it can bring. It’s also time for an update from Adam Frost’s new garden, where things are slowly starting to take shape. In Cumbria, a couple of growers share their love of auriculas as they get ready for this year’s RHS Chelsea Flower Show. And as part of Mental Health Awareness Week, a forager explains how her garden helped her to heal after being diagnosed with cancer.

programme.title: Hidden Treasures of the National Trust
programme.desc: From a fragile silk robe and a wartime wall painting to a writer’s handmade timepiece, the hidden treasures in these two houses reveal the stories of two of Britain’s most celebrated authors – and the expert teams racing to preserve them.

programme.title: Live at the Apollo
programme.desc: At the forefront of its genre, the roll call of stand-ups who have performed in front of the famous Live at the Apollo lights plays out like a who's who of comedic royalty, and this series is no different. Each episode will see a national (and sometimes international!) stand-up both compering and performing, before introducing two of the best established and up-coming stand-ups to the stage. This episode of the award-winning Live at the Apollo is hosted by the awesome Sindhu Vee as she introduces rising comedy star Alex Edelman and the fantastic Lou Sanders to the stage. Other acts to appear throughout the series include Tom Allen, Rosie Jones, Kae Kurd, Darren Harriott, Jessica Fostekew, Stephen Bailey, Desiree Burch, Paul McCaffrey, Jonny Pelham, Ardal O'Hanlon, Sara Barron, Mawaan Rizwan, Guz Khan, Kiri Pritchard-McLean, Rhys James, Sara Pascoe, Chris McCausland and Flo & Joan.

programme.title: Newsnight
programme.desc: Insights and global interviews on the crucial news stories of the day. With Matt Chorley.

programme.title: Triangle of Sadness
programme.desc: Models Carl and Yaya are navigating the world of fashion while exploring the boundaries of their relationship. The couple are invited for a luxury cruise with a rogues’ gallery of super-rich passengers, a Russian oligarch, British arms dealers and an idiosyncratic, alcoholic, Marx-quoting captain. But a storm is brewing, and the cruise ends catastrophically. Carl and Yaya find themselves marooned on a desert island with a group of billionaires and one of the ship’s cleaners. The hierarchy is suddenly flipped upside down, as the housekeeper is the only one who knows how to fish.

programme.title: Interior Design Masters with Alan Carr
programme.desc: The eight remaining designers pair up to create uplifting spaces for a homelessness charity in London. They tackle an arts and crafts room, a group workshop room, a wellness area and an employment suite. The charity’s ambassador, Dara Ó Briain, joins Alan to check in on the designers before Michelle and guest judge Sophie Robinson critique the spaces.

programme.title: The Cage
programme.desc: Matty flails as Ning continues to push him. Meanwhile, Leanne and Gary bond, until he pressures Leanne to betray Matty to safeguard her family.

programme.title: This is BBC Two
programme.desc: Highlights of programmes on BBC Two.

programme.title: Escape to the Country
programme.desc: Nicki Chapman is in stunning south west Wales, helping Carol, along with her husband, return to the country where she grew up. With her son Greg supporting her on the house hunt, she’s dreaming of a home close to the sea. The property line-up includes a picture-perfect double-fronted house with roses around the door, and a mystery house boasting spectacular mountain views... it’s Wales at its most wonderful.

programme.title: Great Central Asian Railway Journeys
programme.desc: Michael Portillo’s railway tour through Uzbekistan continues in the lush oasis surrounding the historic city of Samarkand. Here, he uncovers the Central Asian origins of the apple, a fruit that travelled to Europe along the Silk Road. Exploring vast orchards, he witnesses how millions of apples are grown and processed here each year. Boarding a high-speed train along the old Trans-Caspian Railway, Michael hears how the Russians toiled to build this remarkable line through the shifting sands of Uzbekistan’s steppe. In Bukhara, he explores the faded magnificence of an abandoned Russian imperial palace. He then enters the city’s Islamic heart, and standing in the shadow of the Ark, the city's striking fortified citadel, he unearths the deadly intrigue between Britain and Russia in what became known as the Great Game - and discovers the fate of two British officers thrown into the infamous 'bug pit'.

programme.title: Just One Thing
programme.desc: Clive Myrie is in Kent with Tracey, a soon-to-be grandmother who is worried about her high blood pressure. His suggestion? Borrow a pet – yes, really. With new apps making it simple to match people with animals, Tracey could enjoy all the benefits without the long-term commitment. And the science is clear: spending time with animals boosts happiness, improves wellbeing and lowers the risk of dying from cardiovascular disease. A furry friend might be just what her heart needs.

programme.title: Ronan Keating's Wild Atlantic
programme.desc: Ronan completes this leg of his journey along Ireland's Wild Atlantic in County Derry/Londonderry. He walks the 400-year-old walls of the city with comedian Diona Doherty, and hits the farm to find out just what it takes to be a competitive sheep herder, before heading for the windswept coastline of Castlerock to meet a skilled craft worker who builds traditional coracle boats by hand.

programme.title: BBC News
programme.desc: Twenty-four hours a day, the latest national and international stories as they break.

programme.title: Political Thinking with Nick Robinson
programme.desc: Miatta Fahnbulleh, the first minister to walk out of Keir Starmer’s government since the May elections, talks about mistakes in Downing Street, the PM’s leadership and why she is backing Andy Burnham.

programme.title: Impossible
programme.desc: Game show in which 24 players compete across the series, scoring points by answering questions correctly. However, they must avoid the impossible answers, otherwise they will be eliminated from the show until the next day. In each episode there are three rounds, and the three highest scorers from each round play against each other in the final. The winner of this battle faces a £10,000 question.

programme.title: Mastermind
programme.desc: The hunt for the nation's Mastermind continues as Clive Myrie tests four more contenders on their specialist subjects and general knowledge. The specialist subjects are Marie Curie, the BBC sitcom Ghosts, Elizabeth Woodville and Banksy.

programme.title: Lightning
programme.desc: Comedian Zoe Lyons presents the electrifyingly fast quiz with a £3,000 jackpot. Six plucky contestants compete across six rounds testing their general knowledge, quick thinking and speedy reactions whilst our ruthless spotlight patrols the studio. The contestants’ motivation in each round is simple: stay out of the light and you’ll be alright!

programme.title: Clean It, Fix It
programme.desc: Olivia lives in a one-bedroom flat in London, where every inch of floor space counts, so the team turn her tired and unloved courtyard into an extra living space with some clever storage solutions.

programme.title: Super Smart Animals
programme.desc: For centuries, the idea of intelligent animals struck most people as ridiculous. But not any more - the latest science reveals that animals are a lot smarter than we thought. In the second of two programmes, Liz Bonnin embarks on a worldwide search for the planet's most intelligent animals. Liz meets grey whales with emotions much like our own, unravels how the Caribbean's cleverest monkeys outwit their human neighbours, and even has a conversation with the world's cleverest chimp - with some surprising consequences. Explore how Seattle's crows can hold grudges for years, discover that the cleverest dogs can learn over 1,000 words, and find out why Asian elephants can spend hours looking at themselves in giant mirrors. Then there is meerkat school, eye-poking capuchin armies, and even a new version of Einstein's infamous equation written by a sheepdog. Prepare to be amazed, entertained, and even outwitted by the world's Super Smart Animals.

programme.title: Antiques Roadshow
programme.desc: Michael Aspel invites members of the public to bring along their antiques for examination. The team travel to the northernmost point of Great Britain to visit Shetland. Among the objects that turn up are a valuable enamelled 18th century glass, a painting of a local man by the celebrated railway artist Terence Cuneo, a rare 18th century Chinese 'Ho' pot and a Scottish pearl set in a gold ring.

programme.title: Flog It!
programme.desc: This episode comes from Tilbury Docks in Essex, where antiques experts Elizabeth Talbot and Philip Serrell search for items to take off to auction. Elizabeth finds a mint toy car collection, and Philip unearths a trench periscope from the First World War. Paul Martin uncovers the explosive history of Britain’s biggest gunpowder factory.

programme.title: Richard Osman's House of Games
programme.desc: Every day this week, celebrity contestants Deirdre O'Kane, Jay Rayner, Tessa Sanderson and Iwan Thomas take on a series of quiz rounds selected by the host, quiz legend Richard Osman. A daily winner is declared following a quickfire round at the end of each show, and the scores are tallied across the week, resulting in an overall champion being crowned on Friday. Will the winning stars opt for the much-coveted House of Games decanter, or will they be tempted by the House of Games retro bag?

programme.title: Flog It!
programme.desc: This episode comes from Tilbury Docks in Essex, where antiques experts Elizabeth Talbot and Philip Serrell search for items to take off to auction. Elizabeth finds a mint toy car collection, and Philip unearths a trench periscope from the First World War. Paul Martin uncovers the explosive history of Britain’s biggest gunpowder factory.

programme.title: Richard Osman's House of Games
programme.desc: Every day this week, celebrity contestants Deirdre O'Kane, Jay Rayner, Tessa Sanderson and Iwan Thomas take on a series of quiz rounds selected by the host, quiz legend Richard Osman. programme.title: Great Central Asian Railway Journeys
programme.desc: Michael Portillo’s railway adventure through Uzbekistan reaches its finale in the historic city of Bukhara. Amidst the medieval Islamic architecture, Michael goes in search of a centuries-old Jewish community. Stepping inside a 420-year-old synagogue and a family home, he’s introduced to unique customs and traditions, and a fragrant green dish that has made Bukharan Jews famous worldwide. Michael grapples with kurash, an ancient form of upright wrestling once used to select the bravest warriors and now also increasingly popular as a sport for young Uzbek women. Michael’s exploration of Uzbekistan culminates in the vast Kyzylkum Desert, where he experiences the life of nomadic tribes who once roamed its vast sandy plains. His Central Asian journey concludes among the horses and riders who brave all to take part in one of the most dangerous equestrian sports in the world.

programme.title: Greatest Gardens with Diarmuid Gavin and Carol Klein
programme.desc: Carol Klein and Diarmuid Gavin lead the search along with guest judge and keen gardener Katie Piper to find Northern Ireland’s greatest garden. Up first is Colin’s surprising suburban rustic garden in suburban Ballymena. In the foothills of the Sperrin Mountains, near the windswept Glenshane Pass, Adrienne has transformed two acres using a variety of planting styles. The final stop is in Dromore, where Julietta has created a garden designed with her young family very much in mind, including a wild meadow playground and a courtyard filled with edible plants. There are mixed opinions at the judging table – so which will expert judges Diarmuid, Carol and Katie feel deserves a place in the Greatest Garden final?

programme.title: Beechgrove Garden
programme.desc: It's time for some early summer colour as Carole Baxter makes the first of her visits to classic Scottish gardens. She visits Glenarn, which has a fabulous collection of rhododendrons looking their best right now. Back at Beechgrove Garden, George Anderson and Calum Clunie are busy refreshing the grass and gravel plot and planting new varieties. Calum demonstrates how to take cuttings from a fuchsia, and there are some ideas on how to manage your plot if you are unlucky enough to have club root in your vegetable patch. And there are all the usual handy hints.

programme.title: Gardeners' World
programme.desc: With the promise of warmer days ahead, Monty makes a start on planting up some of his spectacular summer containers. He’s also got leeks to plant out and shares some advice on how to make your own fertiliser. Frances Tophill heads to Berkshire to learn more about biodynamic gardening and the benefits it can bring. It’s also time for an update from Adam Frost’s new garden, where things are slowly starting to take shape. In Cumbria, a couple of growers share their love of auriculas as they get ready for this year’s RHS Chelsea Flower Show. And as part of Mental Health Awareness Week, a forager explains how her garden helped her to heal after being diagnosed with cancer.

programme.title: Hidden Treasures of the National Trust
programme.desc: From a fragile silk robe and a wartime wall painting to a writer’s handmade timepiece, the hidden treasures in these two houses reveal the stories of two of Britain’s most celebrated authors – and the expert teams racing to preserve them.

programme.title: Live at the Apollo
programme.desc: At the forefront of its genre, the roll call of stand-ups who have performed in front of the famous Live at the Apollo lights plays out like a who's who of comedic royalty, and this series is no different. Each episode will see a national (and sometimes international!) stand-up both compering and performing, before introducing two of the best established and up-coming stand-ups to the stage. This episode of the award-winning Live at the Apollo is hosted by the awesome Sindhu Vee as she introduces rising comedy star Alex Edelman and the fantastic Lou Sanders to the stage. Other acts to appear throughout the series include Tom Allen, Rosie Jones, Kae Kurd, Darren Harriott, Jessica Fostekew, Stephen Bailey, Desiree Burch, Paul McCaffrey, Jonny Pelham, Ardal O'Hanlon, Sara Barron, Mawaan Rizwan, Guz Khan, Kiri Pritchard-McLean, Rhys James, Sara Pascoe, Chris McCausland and Flo & Joan.

programme.title: Newsnight
programme.desc: Insights and global interviews on the crucial news stories of the day. With Matt Chorley.

programme.title: Triangle of Sadness
programme.desc: Models Carl and Yaya are navigating the world of fashion while exploring the boundaries of their relationship. The couple are invited for a luxury cruise with a rogues’ gallery of super-rich passengers, a Russian oligarch, British arms dealers and an idiosyncratic, alcoholic, Marx-quoting captain. But a storm is brewing, and the cruise ends catastrophically. Carl and Yaya find themselves marooned on a desert island with a group of billionaires and one of the ship’s cleaners. The hierarchy is suddenly flipped upside down, as the housekeeper is the only one who knows how to fish.

programme.title: Interior Design Masters with Alan Carr
programme.desc: The eight remaining designers pair up to create uplifting spaces for a homelessness charity in London. They tackle an arts and crafts room, a group workshop room, a wellness area and an employment suite. The charity’s ambassador, Dara Ó Briain, joins Alan to check in on the designers before Michelle and guest judge Sophie Robinson critique the spaces.

programme.title: The Cage
programme.desc: Matty flails as Ning continues to push him. Meanwhile, Leanne and Gary bond, until he pressures Leanne to betray Matty to safeguard her family.

programme.title: This is BBC Two
programme.desc: Highlights of programmes on BBC Two.

programme.title: Escape to the Country
programme.desc: Nicki Chapman is in stunning south west Wales, helping Carol, along with her husband, return to the country where she grew up. With her son Greg supporting her on the house hunt, she’s dreaming of a home close to the sea. The property line-up includes a picture-perfect double-fronted house with roses around the door, and a mystery house boasting spectacular mountain views... it’s Wales at its most wonderful.

programme.title: Great Central Asian Railway Journeys
programme.desc: Michael Portillo’s railway tour through Uzbekistan continues in the lush oasis surrounding the historic city of Samarkand. Here, he uncovers the Central Asian origins of the apple, a fruit that travelled to Europe along the Silk Road. Exploring vast orchards, he witnesses how millions of apples are grown and processed here each year. Boarding a high-speed train along the old Trans-Caspian Railway, Michael hears how the Russians toiled to build this remarkable line through the shifting sands of Uzbekistan’s steppe. In Bukhara, he explores the faded magnificence of an abandoned Russian imperial palace. He then enters the city’s Islamic heart, and standing in the shadow of the Ark, the city's striking fortified citadel, he unearths the deadly intrigue between Britain and Russia in what became known as the Great Game - and discovers the fate of two British officers thrown into the infamous 'bug pit'.

programme.title: Just One Thing
programme.desc: Clive Myrie is in Kent with Tracey, a soon-to-be grandmother who is worried about her high blood pressure. His suggestion? Borrow a pet – yes, really. With new apps making it simple to match people with animals, Tracey could enjoy all the benefits without the long-term commitment. And the science is clear: spending time with animals boosts happiness, improves wellbeing and lowers the risk of dying from cardiovascular disease. A furry friend might be just what her heart needs.

programme.title: Ronan Keating's Wild Atlantic
programme.desc: Ronan completes this leg of his journey along Ireland's Wild Atlantic in County Derry/Londonderry. He walks the 400-year-old walls of the city with comedian Diona Doherty, and hits the farm to find out just what it takes to be a competitive sheep herder, before heading for the windswept coastline of Castlerock to meet a skilled craft worker who builds traditional coracle boats by hand.

programme.desc: Duggee masters his ambition of building a model of the Clubhouse out of sticks, so the Squirrels start to think about what their ambitions might be. Norrie wants to learn how to break dance. Happy has always wanted to jump the famous triple puddle splash. Betty has always wanted to teach Mr Cuddles how to speak Portuguese. Roly has loads, from growing a potato to becoming a pirate. Tag spends a long time thinking what his could be, and then it clicks - he needs to climb over the log! Duggee gets to work helping all of the Squirrels train so they can reach their goals. Duggee teaches them that while it may be hard, the important thing is to keep trying and eventually you’ll get there. The Squirrels achieve their ambitions, and Tag successfully climbs over the log. Now they have achieved their first ambitions, the Squirrels can continue to reach for the stars. programme.title: Bing
programme.desc: Coco discovers Bing's dressing-up box so they both dress up. Coco is Princess Cococapono and Bing is, of course, King Bing. programme.title: Yakka Dee!
programme.desc: Dee encourages a friend to say ‘squirrel’, and we go on a whirlwind word adventure. We see lots of different squirrels – grey, red and one with a very bushy tail. Some friends find scampering squirrels, we see a flying one and a supersquirrel wearing a cape! The journey is repeated with some special surprises along the way, and everyone has a boogie when Dee’s friend finally succeeds in saying today’s word.

programme.title: Lu & the Bally Bunch

programme.title: Froglets
programme.desc: On a chilly day, the Froglets enjoy camping outside with a tent, jumpers and marshmallows.

programme.title: Twirlywoos
programme.desc: The Twirlywoos are in a bathroom where they watch a man running a bath, into which he puts some colourful bath salts. The Twirlywoos keep trying to reach the jar of bath salts but are interrupted by the man constantly coming and going with more things for his bath. In the end they reach the bath salts just as the Hooter calls them home. As they fly away, they knock the whole jar into the bath, and the man returns to find his bath overflowing with bubbles! The Stop-Go Car comes to visit the boat and brings the Twirlywoos a balloon. No sooner has he arrived than he is out the door again, and the Twirlywoos watch him drive back across the beach. He keeps coming and going, bringing more balloons each time, until Chickedy and Chick, who are holding all the balloons, start to float away! Only the combined weight of all the Twirlywoos brings them back down, and the balloons escape out of the door.

programme.title: Something Special

programme.title: Teletubbies
programme.desc: The voice trumpet leads a game of I Spy where the Teletubbies have to spot different colours - purple, green, yellow and red. What or who can they spot with those colours?

programme.title: The Baby Club
programme.desc: Nigel and Baby Bear welcome babies Ferne, Tobias, Betsy, Leo, Noah, Holly and their grown-ups to The Baby Club. Inside everyone’s bags in this episode are Plastic Bottles which are explored through discovery, play, song and story. Grown-ups at home are encouraged to take part by hiding safe, baby appropriate plastic bottles inside a fabric bag or pillowcase for them to reveal and explore with their baby! The fun nursery rhyme ‘Five Green Bottles’ features, as does a story involving Baby Bear. Plus, the Action Song gets everyone moving about, before some calm time with bubbles and the Goodbye Song.

programme.title: Monster Makes
programme.desc: Murphi’s comic reading is disturbed by some fluffy fairy dust. Rebecca finds a muffin case, inspiring Murphi’s first make – a muffin case house. Still unable to find the fluffy fairy, Murphi decides it is time for a mega monster make. The Recycling Express arrives with an old tea box, which is transformed into a box dragon, with a little assistance from the Tiny Helpers.

programme.title: Vegesaurs
programme.desc: It's so cold in the Valley that the Pea-Rexes risk becoming frozen!

programme.title: Bluey

programme.title: Maddie's Do You Know?
programme.desc: In today's episode, Maddie is at home to show us how a refrigerator works. She explains how the pump and the long pipes inside a fridge change a cooling liquid into a gas to help the food inside stay cold. Using a special thermal camera we see how food cools down inside. Next, Maddie heads to a mushroom farm to see how mushrooms are grown in a big factory. We see how the climate is controlled by a computer so the mushrooms can grow indoors all year round. Maddie uses a special camera to show us the microscopic spores that grow into mushrooms.

programme.title: Dog Squad
programme.desc: Newfoundland Sylvie is a therapy dog with big soft cuddles who loves to help people when they’re worried. She and her owner Katrina visit all sorts of people every day, young and old. It’s Sylvie and Katrina’s day off, and they’re planning a special lunch at the park café. At the bus stop, they meet Dawn from the toy shop, who is worried that her bus is running late. But seeing Sylvie waiting calmly inspires Dawn to do the same. At the park, Katrina and Sylvie bump into Harry the baker, literally! Harry is worried too; his shop oven isn’t working. Sylvie nuzzles him in support. Grateful for their help, Harry offers Sylvie and Katrina a cake. Then, they meet Pete the postie, who is helping his daughter Caitlin ride her balance bike for the first time. Katrina suggests that Sylvie walks alongside Caitlin as she finds her confidence. Before long, Caitlin is loving every moment. Katrina and Sylvie finally arrive at the park café, only to find that it’s closed. Sylvie summons her super heart and the friends they’ve met along the way to comfort Katrina and to show her that when you’re kind to others, they’re often kind to you in return.

programme.title: Go Wild
programme.desc: Aneeshwar and Lizzie try to meet sunbirds, but they are hard to spot. Fast-moving and tiny, they fly quickly between the branches. When the pair finally catch sight of them, they manage to see these beautifully coloured birds up close. Next, Aneeshwar and Lizzie encounter a day gecko. These amazing lizards are called day geckos because they are normally seen in the daytime. However, they are starting to come out at night to hunt for insects attracted to streetlamps in cities. Finally, Aneeshwar and Lizzie discover what the wild connection is between these two incredible animals.

programme.title: Waffle the Wonder Dog
programme.desc: Waffle is at Mrs Hobbs’ house until the Brooklyn-Bells return from holiday. He acts like a cat to please her and helpfully washes up his bowl, but accidentally leaves the taps on.

programme.title: Puffin Rock

programme.title: Yukee

programme.title: Maddie + Triggs

programme.title: Hey Duggee
programme.desc: Snail is thrilled to be moving house as she wishes to escape the wet and sploshy place she currently calls home for a more spacious house on the hill. But before she can move up in the world, she’s going to need some help from Duggee and the Squirrels to move her many belongings up the hill! Snail can’t do it alone, so Duggee teaches the Squirrels the best ways that they can get moving! They band together, cradling items and shifting furniture. Snail looks on with apprehension as they manage fragile vases with less care than she’d like. Luckily, Duggee intercepts the vases before they crash head first into one another and teaches the Squirrels all the ways they can move to ensure Snail has a stress-free and efficient move. They could lift, push or pull to get things moving! They work together as a team to get the job done before Snail can even reach the house, so they give her a helping hand too.

programme.title: Numberblocks
programme.desc: The animated adventures of friends who can always count on each other. Five arrives to get the band together, and the party started, with a big high five.

programme.title: Alphablocks

They find out that ivy is an evergreen plant, so it provides shelter the whole year round to insects, birds and other animals. They learn that it can also be a food source for lots of creatures, like birds, which eat the ivy’s berries in winter. programme.desc: Dad and his mates hit the backyard ready to rip up some tree stumps!

programme.title: Waffle the Wonder Dog
programme.desc: Doug's tooth has fallen out, so Jess and Simon tell Waffle about the Tooth Fairy. Waffle longs to meet the Tooth Fairy and his dream comes true.
